title: 3D-Polishing for Triangular Mesh Compression of Point Cloud Data

problem.claim: The increasing size of point cloud data and generated triangular meshes creates high computational costs for processing, visualization, analysis, transmission, and storage.

gap.claim: A compression approach is needed that reduces point and triangle counts while maintaining surface approximation quality and preserving global surface features.

contributions.claim: A greedy 3D-polishing algorithm progressively removes redundant points and triangles while maintaining surface approximation quality.
An approximate curvature radius evaluates the scale of features polished at each iteration.

A rank-based procedure formulates compression-rate selection as change-point detection and selects an optimal compression rate intended to preserve most global surface features with statistical guarantee.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the greedy 3D-polishing algorithm as a novel progressive mesh compression approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on moderate- and large-scale 3D shape datasets show substantial reductions in point cloud and triangular mesh size.
The authors report that most surface information can be retained using substantially fewer points and triangles.

narrative_sequence.summary: Triangular meshes are used to reconstruct 3D object surfaces from point cloud data.
Growing point clouds and meshes increase computational costs across data-processing and data-management tasks.
The paper introduces greedy 3D polishing to progressively remove redundant points and triangles while maintaining surface approximation quality.
Approximate curvature radius and rank-based change-point detection support feature-scale evaluation and compression-rate selection.
Experiments on moderate- and large-scale 3D shape datasets report substantial size reduction while retaining most surface information.

source_observation.claim: The method combines progressive greedy simplification with a feature-scale measure and data-driven compression-rate selection.

interpretation.claim: Compression quality may benefit from coordinating local simplification decisions with an explicit criterion for selecting the stopping or compression rate.

application.claim: For geometric data reduction, pair iterative removal with feature-aware monitoring and a principled rule for choosing the final reduction level.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design transfers to geometries, representations, or quality objectives outside the evaluated 3D shape datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the moderate- and large-scale datasets.
Quantitative compression ratios, quality metrics, baselines, and statistical-guarantee details are not provided.
The abstract does not specify computational cost, runtime, or memory results.
Independent verification and reproducibility details are not provided.
